summary.intent: Document the project's non-negotiable invariants (tagged by enforcement type), reconcile them with exceptions the code already has, and have the code conform to the rules by removing violations and dead API.
summary.outcome: PR #54 (docs only, trail 189) was pushed, titled, and marked ready for review. The code-conformance half (removing Serialize from core types, moving the truncation string, deleting dead API) is still running in a separate agent worktree.

repo: Invariants are now tagged [lint], [type] or [convention]; of 11 rules, 2 are lint, 1 is type, and 8 are convention, so most are enforced only by review.
Documented exceptions the code already had: DigestParseError, NonUtf8Path holding a PathBuf, and all modules being pub until the library API is designed (nothing stable before 1.0).
The wildcard-match rule can't be a clippy lint because clippy can't scope it to owned enums.
The rank/ module is hasher-generic and the pipeline passes an FxHashMap, so the no-std-HashMap rule holds; the two apparent std HashMap uses were false positives from the guard script.
The parser.rs:60 wildcard no longer exists after PR #45.
Serialize on the 29 core types is only used by tests, so the code should conform to the rule by removing it.
Work is linked to 'trail 189' and the branch gets a shadow PR (here #54) after being linked.

code.finding: The wildcard match previously flagged here no longer exists after #45, so the audit entry was stale.

workflow: Verify audit findings by hand: the guard script produced false positives (std HashMap in rank/) that would have wrongly flagged a rule as violated.
Re-check PR draft claims before posting; rule counts were wrong and a 'grep found none' claim had not actually been run.
Split docs and code changes into separate PRs, delegating the large code deletion to an agent in its own worktree.
For deletion-heavy refactors, require byte-identical CLI output on fixtures (before and after), a changeset, and a semver check as evidence.
